title: How antibodies lie
objective: Explain how to validate that an antibody stains its intended target.

steps.title: A pretty stain isn't proof
steps.body: A pretty stain doesn't prove the antibody hit the right protein. Antibodies cross-react, bind off-target proteins, and vary by lot. The gold standard: the signal **disappears in a knockout** (or knockdown) that lacks the target.

steps.setup: An antibody gives the same strong stain in wild-type and in the target's knockout tissue.
options: The signal isn't the target — it's off-target or non-specific
This validates the antibody as clean and fully specific
The knockout must somehow still be expressing the protein
steps.reveal: If the stain persists without the target, it isn't reporting the target. A validated antibody loses signal in the knockout.

variants.prompt: A KO tissue stains as brightly as wild-type. The antibody is…
options: Not reporting the target — it's off-target signal
Validated as specific and ready to trust fully
Only usable at a higher working dilution now
variants.explanation: Specific signal should vanish without the target.

steps.prompt: Match each validation approach to what it rules out.
pairs: Signal isn't the target at all
Second antibody to a different epitope
Binding isn't via the intended epitope
steps.explanation: Converging evidence — KO, independent antibody, and blocking — builds trust no single test can.

steps.prompt: Why does the lab confirm marker expression with **[[RNAscope]]** as well as antibodies?
options: An orthogonal method (mRNA) cross-checks the protein stain
RNAscope shows where the protein sits more precisely
RNAscope skips fixation, so epitopes can't be masked
RNAscope needs no experimental controls of its own
steps.explanation: Detecting the mRNA in the same cells is independent support that the antibody marks the right neurons — two methods, one answer.

variants.setup: An antibody stain and RNAscope for the same marker agree.
options: Two independent methods converge on the same cells
It shows the antibody also binds the target's mRNA
It proves the protein is made at high levels there
variants.reveal: Independent methods agreeing is strong evidence the signal is real.

sources.citation: Uhlén M et al., 2016, Nature Methods

sources.note: Uses perfusion-fixed and whole-mount tissue to map colon DRG endings.

reviewNotes: Antibody validation; ties to RNAscope cross-check in the lab.
